content: 1. Each facility being costed should have its own dedicated data entry workbook, which must be locked after data entry is completed. 2. The workbook contains a 'List' sheet that is linked to data throughout the tool, and a 'Notes' sheet that serves as a free space for tracking unresolved issues. The 'Notes' sheet is not linked to other data in the tool. 3. Parameters such as the year of assessment, number of months evaluated, and assumptions about days, weeks, and working hours are predefined and should be validated before locking the sheet. 4. Data for facility characteristics should be copied and pasted into the Data Entry Tool from the data collection workbook. Ensure dropdown selections for additional service output types are properly selected. 5. For building space, calculations for annualized economic and financial costs should be reviewed, including allocations of building costs to direct, support, and indirect facility departments. 6. The useful life of the building, discount rate, and value if sold today are used to calculate annualized costs using a PMT function. 7. Equipment costs should be allocated to TB services using a top-down approach, based on service statistics or the proportion of TB tests performed. If equipment is used for multiple outputs, usage percentages should be split across rows. 8. Staff time allocation should be calculated using either timesheets, interviews, or assumptions. For staff without timesheets, time distribution can be assumed to match that of similar staff within the same cadre. 9. Training data should be TB-related and include details such as the name of the training, location, provider, date, duration, and number of participants. 10. Supplies should be allocated to service outputs based on observations or interviews. Ensure the quantities and costs are correctly pulled from the price list and allocated accurately. 11. Drug quantities and costs should be reviewed, including total annual quantities disbursed for TB and average drugs per patient. 12. Data collection time can be analyzed to assess the time investment in the costing study. This includes time spent collecting data and transferring it to the Data Entry Tool. 13. Service statistics should be reviewed to ensure accurate allocation of main cost components in unit costs. 14. For shared spaces, allocation should be based on TB visits as a proportion of total visits or estimated by staff using the space. 15. Equipment allocation should ideally use the number of tests performed. For specialized equipment like MGIT or Xpert MTB/RIF, time usage can also be included in the calculation. 16. Observations should be the default method for data collection, but interviews may be used if direct observation is not feasible. 17. A pilot study is recommended to test tool adaptation and data availability, taking approximately one week. 18. Ensure all data matches the corresponding sheets in the tool, such as price lists for supplies and equipment. 19. For staff categories, additional staff members can be included in designated spaces, with text changes allowed only in blue-font cells. 20. The tool includes linked lists for healthcare workers and staff, ensuring consistency across sheets. 21. For bottom-up methods, staff time and supply usage should be entered based on observations or interviews, with the method of measurement clearly selected. 22. Drug costs for adverse event treatments are not included in unit costs. 23. Data collection sheets include spaces for start and end dates and times to document the data collection process comprehensively. 24. General supplies and their allocations should be reviewed to ensure accuracy, with economic costs properly distributed. 25. The tool allows for adjustments in time measurement allocation for mixed methods, with a default of 50% observation and 50% interview. 26. Spot checks should be performed to verify that unit prices and cost calculations are accurate and applied to the correct quantities. 27. For laboratory or radiology departments, allocation should be based on the proportion of TB tests to total department tests. 28. If direct measurement of space usage is not possible, use visit data or staff estimates to allocate space for TB versus non-TB services. 29. For equipment used infrequently, such as for MDR-TB testing, interview data may be the only option for allocation. 30. A template for data collector timesheets is included in the tool to facilitate detailed time tracking during data collection.
